acceptance: `evolve loop status` prints the loop's status and starts nothing (red: it launches a batch with goal 'status')
`evolve loop stop` exits 10 and names `evolve loop-stop`
A multi-word positional goal still launches as before
fix: Before flag parsing, dispatch `evolve loop status [--json]` to a read-only report: the loop section of `evolve status` (running, brake, cycle, phase, lease heartbeat). Refuse a positional goal that is exactly a reserved word (status, stop, help, plan, watch) with exit 10, naming the intended verb. Document it in runtime-reference.md's operator commands.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: runLoop parses every positional argument as a cycle count, a strategy or the goal (cmd_loop_args.go:156; parsePositional at :203), and resolveGoal takes a positional string as the goal text (:118-119). So `evolve loop status`, the natural way to ask whether the loop is running, starts a batch whose goal is 'status'. The read-only answer lives in `evolve dashboard --snapshot`.
title: `evolve loop status` launches a loop because the word is parsed as goal text; make it a read-only subcommand and refuse reserved words as goals
